Why should red wine not have equal rights?

Red wine isn’t a person, so “rights” don’t apply to it in the legal or moral sense. But if you mean equal treatment compared with white wine, its color alone is no reason to discriminate—both deserve fair representation at the dinner table.

Why should red wine not have equal rights?

Red wine isn’t a person or sentient being, so “rights” don’t apply to it in the same way they apply to humans. But as a beverage, it should certainly receive equal respect alongside white wine, rosé, and other drinks—unless someone simply prefers another flavor.
